tools.name: extract
tools.description: Fetch any public web page and get clean readable text for LLM input: title, meta description, language, canonical URL, H1-H3 headings, main body text with navigation, scripts and boilerplate removed, and the page's outbound links. Use for web scraping, article reading, research and RAG ingestion. Co

tools.name: domain
tools.description: Domain intelligence in one call: DNS records (A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, NS, TXT, CAA), DNSSEC status, registrar, registration and expiry dates with domain age in days (RDAP/WHOIS), and email authentication (SPF and DMARC records and policies, whether the domain accepts mail). Use for lead qualification, p

tools.name: token
tools.description: Live on-chain facts for any ERC-20 token on Base: name, symbol, decimals, total supply, owner address and whether ownership is renounced, paused state, proxy detection (EIP-1967 and minimal proxy) with implementation and admin addresses, and bytecode heuristics for mint, pause, blacklist and fee-set

tools.name: wallet
tools.description: Live snapshot of any address on Base: ETH balance, balances of major tokens (USDC, WETH, cbBTC, DAI, USDbC, cbETH, AERO, EURC) plus up to 20 extra token addresses you pass, transaction count, and whether the address is an EOA, a smart contract or an EIP-7702 delegated account. Use for portfolio chec

tools.name: summarize
tools.description: Give a URL, get a short summary of the page plus three to six key points, ready to drop into an agent's context. Fetches the page, strips navigation and boilerplate, and summarizes the main text with an LLM. Use for research, news triage, link previews and deciding whether a page is worth reading in

tools.name: screenshot
tools.description: Render any public web page in a real headless Chrome browser, with JavaScript executed, and get a JPEG screenshot (1280 px wide, base64) plus the final URL, HTTP status and page title. Set fullPage=true to capture up to 4000 px of page height. Use for visual checks, page previews, monitoring and fee

tools.name: image
tools.description: Text-to-image generation with FLUX.1 schnell. Send a prompt, get a 1024x1024 JPEG back as base64 in a few seconds. Use for illustrations, thumbnails, mockups, avatars and social media images. Optional steps parameter (1-8, default 4) trades speed for detail. Costs $0.02 in USDC on Base per successfu

tools.name: transcribe
tools.description: Transcribe speech from an audio file at a public URL using Whisper large-v3-turbo. Returns the transcript text, detected language, duration and word count. Accepts common formats such as MP3, WAV, M4A and OGG up to 5 MB. Use for voice notes, podcast clips, meeting snippets and voice messages. Costs

tools.name: describe
tools.description: Vision model for an image at a public URL: get a detailed description including any visible text, or pass a question to ask something specific about the image. Accepts PNG, JPEG, WebP and GIF up to 3 MB. Use for alt text, OCR-style reading of screenshots, chart reading and content checks. Costs $0.0

tools.name: btc-fees
tools.description: Current Bitcoin network fee rates in sat/vB for next-block, half-hour, one-hour and economy confirmation, the estimated cost in sats of a typical payment, mempool size and total pending fees, and the latest block height. Use before sending a Bitcoin transaction or to decide whether to wait for lower

tools.name: btc-address
tools.description: Balance and activity of any Bitcoin mainnet address (legacy, P2SH or bech32): confirmed balance in sats and BTC, unconfirmed pending amount, total received and sent, and transaction counts. Use for payment verification, checking whether a deposit arrived, and wallet monitoring. Costs $0.003 in USDC

tools.name: ln-invoice
tools.description: Decode a BOLT11 Lightning Network invoice without paying it: network, amount in sats and BTC, description, payment hash, creation time, expiry time and whether it has already expired. Use to check what an invoice asks for before an agent pays it. Costs $0.001 in USDC on Base per successful call, pai

tools.name: package
tools.description: Check a software package before installing it: whether it exists at all (AI coding assistants sometimes invent names), latest version and release date, package age, number of versions, weekly downloads (npm), licenses, deprecation, and known security advisories with severity. Returns a verdict of ok

tools.name: email
tools.description: Validate an email address before using it: syntax, whether the domain exists and accepts mail (MX records), disposable or throwaway provider detection, role addresses such as info@ or support@, free-provider detection, and SPF and DMARC presence. Returns a verdict of likely-deliverable, risky, undel

tools.name: papers
tools.description: Search scholarly literature across journals, conferences, preprints and books: title, authors, year, venue, citation count, DOI link and abstract where available. Optional fromYear filter and up to 20 results per call. Use for research agents, literature reviews, fact-checking a claim against publis

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "email" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Validate an email address before using it: syntax, whether the domain exists and accepts mail (MX records), disposable or throwaway provider detection, role add…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: extract, summarize, screenshot, describe, email, papers · Private data: domain, token, wallet, transcribe, btc-address, email · Public sink: domain, image, email · Destructive: summarize.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: extract, summarize, screenshot, describe, email, papers · Private data: domain, token, wallet, transcribe, btc-address, email · Public sink: domain, image, email · Destructive: summarize

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
